Follow audio files through the workflow

Source: R/audio_history.R
pam_audio_history.Rd

Collects, for every audio file, what each stage recorded about it: the standardization result (Stage 0), the scan and QC flags (Stage 1), filtering (Stage 2), detection (Stage 3), cleaning (Stage 4), validation (Stage 5), ground-truth annotation (Stage 5b) and whether it went into the occupancy histories (Stage 6). It reads the files the stages already write, so it works on existing projects and changes nothing unless you ask it to write.

Usage

pam_audio_history(cfg, file = NULL, run_id = NULL, wide = FALSE, write = FALSE)

Arguments

cfg

A pam_config object.

file

Optional audio file to look up: a path relative to the standardized audio folder (such as "G0059/G0059_20260405_183000.wav"), a file name, or, for files standardized by Stage 0, the name of the raw file. NULL (the default) returns every file.

run_id

Optional detection run (or runs). NULL (the default) includes every run found in the project.

wide

If TRUE, return one row per file with one column per stage (and per run, for the stages that belong to a run) holding the status.

write

If TRUE, also save the long table to metadata/audio_history.csv. Nothing is written by default.

Value

A data.table. The long table has one row per file and stage (and run) with columns rel (path relative to the standardized audio folder, NA for files Stage 0 set aside), file (file name), stage, run_id, status, detail (what happened, in words), n (a count, such as the number of detections) and time (when the stage recorded it, where the stage keeps a time, otherwise the time its output file was written). The attribute stages_found lists the stages whose outputs were found. With wide = TRUE the table has rel plus one status column per stage.

Details

Statuses: Stage 0 ok, warning or failed; Stage 1 pass or fail; Stage 2 and 3 ok or failed; Stage 4 kept (some events survived cleaning) or removed (none did); Stage 5 reviewed or sampled; Stage 5b annotated, partly annotated or drawn; Stage 6 included or excluded. Stages whose outputs are missing are skipped. Times are saved in UTC when write = TRUE. The history is built from the current outputs, so a stage you delete or rerun is shown as it now is.

Examples

ex <- pam_example_project()
res <- suppressMessages(pam_scan_audio(ex$cfg))
proc <- suppressMessages(pam_process_detections(ex$cfg))

# one row per file and stage
hist <- pam_audio_history(ex$cfg)
as.data.frame(hist)[1:3, c("file", "stage", "status", "detail")]
#>                        file     stage status        detail
#> 1 G0059_20260405_183000.wav    1 scan   pass  deployment 1
#> 2 G0059_20260405_183000.wav 4 process   kept 2 events kept
#> 3 G0059_20260405_183002.wav    1 scan   pass  deployment 1

# one file, by name
one <- pam_audio_history(ex$cfg, file = "G0059_20260405_183004.wav")
as.data.frame(one)[, c("stage", "status", "detail")]
#>       stage status                                             detail
#> 1    1 scan   pass                                       deployment 1
#> 2 4 process   kept 1 event kept; removed: beyond end of recording (1)

# one row per file, one column per stage
as.data.frame(pam_audio_history(ex$cfg, wide = TRUE))
#>                               rel 1 scan 4 process [run01]
#> 1 G0059/G0059_20260405_183000.wav   pass              kept
#> 2 G0059/G0059_20260405_183002.wav   pass              kept
#> 3 G0059/G0059_20260405_183004.wav   pass              kept
#> 4 G0110/G0110_20260406_060000.wav   pass              kept
#> 5 G0110/G0110_20260406_060002.wav   pass              kept
#> 6 G0110/G0110_20260406_060004.wav   pass           removed
